title: Shortest Distance from All Buildings
description:
You are given an `m x n` grid `grid` of values `0`, `1`, or `2`, where:
- `0` marks an empty land that you can pass through freely.
- `1` marks a building that you cannot pass through.
- `2` marks an obstacle that you cannot pass through.

You want to build a single house on an empty land that reaches all buildings in the shortest total travel distance. You can only move up, down, left, and right.

Return the minimum total travel distance to reach all buildings. If it is not possible to build such a house according to the above rules, return `-1`.

examples.explanation: Building the house at (1,2) has distances 3 + 3 + 1 = 7 to the 3 buildings.
The only empty space is adjacent to the single building.

constraints: There will be at least one building in the grid.
hints: Start BFS from each building (1) rather than from each empty land (0), because usually buildings < empty lands.
Accumulate distance in totalDist[r][c] and increment reach[r][c] count.
After all BFS traversals, find the minimum totalDist[r][c] where reach[r][c] == total_buildings.
